subject: Can STAN handle probabilistic inclusion of data in subsets used for parameter estimation?

messages.author: 2567ef0395c70306
messages.subject: Can STAN handle probabilistic inclusion of data in subsets used for parameter estimation?
parts:
Hi STAN users,

   I'm trying to transition a somewhat complicated modeling exercise from JAGS to STAN, in hopes that STAN can do a better job of exploring posterior distributions of some complex relationships between variables and datasets. Essentially, I'm trying to conduct a meta-analysis of the effect of temperature on pathogen die-off rates in water, combining data from many experiments in the literature. Traditionally, this has been modeled like so:

ln(C(t)_i)~Normal(ln(C(0)_i)-k_i*t, sigma_C)

k_i~Normal(k_20*exp(lambda*(T_i-20)), sigma_k)

Where C(t)_i is the concentration of organisms at time t in experiment i, C(0)_i is the initial concentration, k_i is the geometric rate of die-off, k_20 is the mean rate of die-off at a reference temperature of 20 degrees Celsius, T_i is the temperature at which experiment i was conducted, and lambda is a coefficient for geometric increases in the rate of decay with temperature.

What I'm eventually trying to accomplish is an extension of this model to a typical non(log) linear decay pattern. For many microbes, a tailing off of the rate of die-off is common, giving the appearance of two distinct populations decaying at separate rates. This type of biphasic decay is usually modeled as a sum of two exponential decay functions:

ln(C(t)_i)~Normal(ln(C(0)_i)+ln(a_i*exp(-k1_i*t)+(1-a_i)*exp(-k2_i*t)), sigma_C)

k1_i~Normal(k1_20*exp(lambda1*(T_i-20)), sigma_k1)
k2_i~Normal(k2_20*exp(lambda2*(T_i-20)), sigma_k2)

where k1 is the decay rate for the more sensitive subpopulation, k2 is the decay rate for the more resistant subpopulation, and a is the proportion of organisms belonging to the sensitive population subject to k1.

In the context of a meta-analysis, there is the added challenge to the second model that some data exhibit biphasic decay and some do not. To cope with this, I'm pursuing the assumption that the temperature dependencies of k1 and k2 underlie the temperature dependency of monophasic decay, following from the idea that monophasic data can represent either the case where only the sensitive or resistant subpopulations were present, or both populations were present, but poor resolution/measurement errors resulted in an inability to resolve the biphasic decay. My model for combining biphasic and monophasic data would use biphasic experiments to estimate the temperature responses of k1 and k2, then, for monophasic experiments, use a discrete categorical variable to assign monophasic rate constant k to either the temperature-dependent distribution of k1 or k2, in which case a=1 or a=0 and the monophasic data impact the posterior distribution of the biphasic temperature response functions. Alternatively, k can be assigned to a third category, in which case it is drawn from a diffuse, non-temperature dependent prior distribution, and a is estimated between 0 and 1 based on the relative values of k, and k1 and k2 at the given temperature. In this case, the monophasic data are not used to estimate temperature dependency of k1 and k2. Is it reasonable to pursue this model in STAN, or is this sort of dynamic inclusion of data for parameter estimates incompatible with STAN's form of inference?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can STAN handle probabilistic inclusion of data in subsets used for parameter estimation?
parts:
Hi. That question was really hard to follow, so short answer, yes.

The long answer: yes. But I don't see what part of this has "dynamic inclusion of data"? What does that mean? If you can write down a (log) joint probability function for the data and the parameters, then this is straightforward.



Daniel

messages.author: 2567ef0395c70306
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can STAN handle probabilistic inclusion of data in subsets used for parameter estimation?
parts:
Hi Krzyzsztof and Daniel,

   Thanks for the replies and sorry for the confusing question. I'll work on figuring out the joint probability function. What I meant by dynamic inclusion of data was that if the categorical variable assigns a set of monophasic data to either of the temperature dependent probability distributions for the biphasic rate parameters, then the data influences the estimation of those temperature-dependent probability distributions. If the experiment is assigned to the third (intermediate) category, then the data doesn't influence the underlying temperature dependent probability distributions.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can STAN handle probabilistic inclusion of data in subsets used for parameter estimation?
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm still having trouble with the jargon.

If the inclusion is based on data alone, then no problem.
If the inclusion is based on parameter values, then you're really looking at a mixture model and you should look at the section on marginalizing discrete parameters.



Daniel

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can STAN handle probabilistic inclusion of data in subsets used for parameter estimation?
parts:
Exactly.  If the inclusion depends on parameters then you
naively require some latent categorical variable which would
require integer-valued states in the Markov chain which is
not allowed in Stan.  But you can include all possible 
configurations of data at once with a mixture model, using
Stan to explore the (continuous) mixing weights.
